descriptionHtml:
Bug B18 · P1 · known

Many dates and times follow the device clock instead of server time (UAT 3.8): 'NEW TODAY', admit date, vitals date, task done time, transcript date; with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it

Tickets: TFA-92584 ready for qa (UAT 3.8); TFA-92597 ready for qa (R6); TFA-92579 AC 3/4 ready for qa (NEW TODAY); TFA-94745 ready for qa (draft restore) · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local

Note: Root cause known (Daniela asked for server time on 10-03); the deleted drug, missing badge and wrong draft restore are new symptoms. TC-16/S18 (UAT 3.8, one device set to the wrong date): a phone a day ahead files its bedside line in a row dated tomorrow on the shared record, and the next write from a correctly clocked device lists the lines before it twice (the transcript archive trusts the device date). Which calendar day a correct device should use when its local day and the server's UTC day differ is the open question Q9 (D10); TC-16/S25 passed otherwise. Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579/92584): a browser whose day is ahead writes the badge roll back to the server, and every device shows Follow-up, with the matching template and billing family (TC-01/S08, TC-20/S20a; TFA-92584 AC 8). The failing cell of TC-25/S24a is the card's NEW TODAY, which compares addedAt with the device's date (PatientCard.tsx:154-156). EFS/S28 (a)(b) restore drafts by the device date (TFA-94745); (c), an old draft put in today's box, is B13's. Review 2026-10-15 (TFA-94514): the analytics day is the device date too (pilotUsageEvents / pilotDailyRounding use localDay()): a phone 3 days ahead files its rows under its own day, and an encounter across the phone midnight is split over two days and never timed (OAT-06/S10). Re-test 2026-10-16 (TC-21/S26, 25acd727): a browser two days ahead writes the badge roll with its own future day (encTypeDay 2026-10-19) to the shared record, so the correct-clock browser shows Follow-up too.

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S08, TC-10/S22, TC-12/S23, TC-19/S19, TC-22/S23, TC-25/S24a, TC-02/S13b, EFS/S28, TC-16/S18, TC-06/S19, OAT-06/S10, TC-06/S23, TC-21/S22, TC-25/S24b, TC-21/S26

Approach · TC-19 Medication Tracker · S23 Real dictation of medication changes on iPhone and Android, both contexts

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U18 The step mix (starts, holds, stops, dose changes, conditional orders, one-time doses) is dictated across two days and passes in both Hospital and Nursing Home. (UAT TC-19 Steps; UAT 3.3)
  • U21 Each run records which model did the pre-round processing and the medication-event extraction (and the speech-to-text engine for dictation), and logs the AI call's own time separately from the total. (UAT 3.1; UAT 3.5; UAT 3.9)
  • U23 Server day for the dates the tracker writes: a hold/stop/start tag ('Held · Mon D'), a row's updatedAt and the chart's medicationsUpdatedAt follow the server's day and time, whatever the device clock … (UAT 3.8; TFA-92597 R6 (hold/stop keeps its date))

Test design technique: Device (device) — Look at the layout and gestures at phone size or on a real device (iPhone / Pixel).

Given Debug builds from round-companion-wt-qa on real phones, pointed at the local stack (.env.mobile.local VITE_CONVEX_URL = the Mac's LAN address on port 4510; Android emulator 10.0.2.2:4510; capacitor.config.ts says LAN backends belong there), signed in to an e2e-fresh @roundai.test account. …

When Dictate S07's encounter text (Hospital) and S08's save-2 text (Nursing Home) with the microphone, then Save & Extract / Save Note. Last line (moved from S19): set one phone's date 2 days back and its time zone to UTC-10, Save & Extract 'Hold lisinopril, BP soft.' and compare the Held tag with the server's day

Then Drug names and numbers transcribed correctly; the tracker and panel end as in S07 / S08; the speech-to-text engine used is recorded (GPT-Live; Deepgram only with ambient on); the wrong-clock phone shows the server's date on the Held tag

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Tester compares the transcript and rows with S07/S08's expected results; engine from the run log (3.9). Any run that would need the store build or the dev deployment is not done here: it needs Quinn's explicit go first (needs-dev-or-prod)

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method DEVICE · Real device (iOS / Android); lane planned in the matrix: manual (manual)

S23 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-19.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 0 rows.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 25acd727 (10-15/16 re-tests), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: DEVICE · Real device (iOS / Android) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: newspec-c.

UAT item: TC-19 Medication Tracker · Section: A4 · Post-Round · Scenario: TC-19/S23

Real dictation of medication changes on iPhone and Android, both contexts

Tickets: TFA-92597 Medication Tracker (ready for qa)

New local lane newspec-c: status failed in newspec-c/results.json → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue; part of it is a known gap)).

Detail:

Android rig: debug build of main e02167f bundled for the LOCAL stack only (bundle names 127.0.0.1:4510/4511, reached through adb reverse), built outside the checkout, on the rc_api36 emulator (Pixel 7, Android 16); Playwright attached to the app's own WebView; every ai/* action the app sends is answered or failed at the WebView's socket (no model call; aiCallLog had no new row in any run). Our addition (10-15 review), but data is lost, so it counts. Typed 'Hold lisinopril, BP soft.' + Save & Extract on a phone set two days back in Pacific/Honolulu (the hold answered at the socket). The phone shows 'Held · Oct 12' (its own date; the server's day is Oct 14 UTC / Oct 15 JST) and medicationsUpdatedAt was stored as 2026-10-12. When the correctly set web device then opened the chart, the lisinopril row was gone from the server and the web showed no Held tag at all. This is known B18 ('with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it'). Left: dictating the S07/S08 medication changes with a real voice on real phones (transcription accuracy, engine).

Product issue: A hold entered on a phone whose date is two days behind is stamped two days back; the next time a correctly set device opens the chart the held medication disappears from the tracker (known B18).

Known gap (known): true

Evidence: 4 attached.

Dev run: skipped: set-aside — set-aside: iOS/Android; dictation by microphone/speaker (Quinn 2026-10-14) — Real dictation of medication changes by microphone on iPhone and Android, and a phone with a wrong date: microphone/speaker, iOS and Android are set aside for the dev run (Quinn 2026-10-14).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
